svg.title: Ishikari metro map, readable

g.title: Ishikari metro map: How to read this map. Click for more.
g.text: Read it clockwise, from Task at the top.

g.title: Part 1: 1 ASK · 2 PLAN Click for more.
Part 2: 3 BUILD · 4 CHECK · 5 FIX · 6 MERGE Click for more.
Part 3: 6 FINISH: JUDGE · MAIN MOVES Click for more.
Plan line: The first stretch of the ring: from your task to the worker plans. Click for more.
Question line: The investigator asks you, you answer. Click for more.
Research line: The investigator sends researcher ants. Click for more.
Build line: The long stretch of the ring: build, check, merge, judge, finish. Click for more.
Fix loop: A bug goes back to the worker and is re-checked. Click for more.
Clash line: Tasks that break together go back to the fix loop. Click for more.
Dropped spur: A task that could not be fixed leaves here. Click for more.
Merge failed spur: A failed merge goes back to the worker ants. Click for more.
Cleanup failed spur: A failed cleanup becomes a suggested next task. Click for more.
Judge fix loop: Below 7 with gaps: one fix round. Click for more.
After main moves: Green: the run's work is on main. Click for more.
Check failed spur: A failed app check starts one new task. Click for more.
Fast path: A trivial task skips the planning and build ants: straight across the ring to MAIN. Click for more.
Merge failed spur: merge failed: to Worker ants s8 Click for more.
g.text: merge failed: to Worker ants s8

g.title: Junction: Where the dropped spur leaves the line. Click for more.
Dropped spur: dropped Click for more.
Cleanup failed spur: cleanup failed: to Task s1 (next run) Click for more.
g.text: cleanup failed: to Task s1 (next run)

g.title: Check failed spur: check failed: to Worker ants s8 (new task) Click for more.
g.text: check failed: to Worker ants s8 (new task)

g.title: Fast path: fast path: to MAIN s21 Click for more.
Junction: Where the judge fix loop rejoins the line. Click for more.
Task (s1): The work you hand Ishikari. Click for more.
Investigator ant (s2): Asks you questions, then designs the task and writes every plan. Click for more.
You (s3): You answer the investigator's questions. Click for more.
Researcher ants (s4): Look up facts for the investigator. Click for more.
investigation_report.md (s5): Everything learned while planning, written once. Click for more.
architecture.md (s6): The investigator's design, so parallel workers fit together. Click for more.
Worker plans (s7): One complete plan per task. Click for more.
Worker ants (s8): Build the plans, one worktree each. Click for more.
Detective ants (s9): Check each built task and plan every fix. Click for more.
Integrator ant (s10): Merges all passing tasks in a scratch copy and tests once. Click for more.
Merger ant (s11): Merges the approved tasks for real, then checks with git; failures go back to the workers. Click for more.
Janitor ant (s12): Cleans up mess the run left, by itself. Click for more.
Juror ants (s13): Score each merged task against its plan. Click for more.
Judge ant (s14): Scores the whole run 0-10 against the plans. Click for more.
Worker ant (s15): Closes the judge's gaps. Click for more.
Detective ant (s16): Checks the judge fix. Click for more.
Merger ant (s17): Lands the judge fix by fast-forward. Click for more.
Judge ant (s18): Scores again after the fix. Click for more.
Docs ant (s19): Updates the repo's docs for the merged tasks, last, on the final code. Click for more.
Finisher ant (s20): Moves main, cleans up, runs the check. Click for more.
MAIN (s21): Your main branch, moved forward. Click for more.
checkCommand (s22): Builds and checks the app after main moves. Click for more.
Retrospective ant (s23): Reviews how this run went and suggests fixes to the Ishikari flow. Read only. Click for more.
Run report (s24): The run ends with one report. Click for more.
Logbook (s25): Every ant's reply, one entry each. Click for more.
Car 1: A sample task riding the plan line. Click for more.
Car 2: A sample task riding the build line. Click for more.
Car 3: A sample task riding the build line. Click for more.
Car 4: A sample task riding the build line. Click for more.
Car 5: A sample task riding the build line. Click for more.
Car 6: A sample task riding the build line. Click for more.
Car 7: A sample task riding the fix loop. Click for more.
Car 8: A sample task riding the fix loop. Click for more.
Car 10: A sample task riding the after main moves. Click for more.
Car 11: A sample task riding the judge fix loop. Click for more.
Moving dot: Shows a round of questions. Click for more.
Moving dot: Shows a burst of research. Click for more.
Key: What the cars, symbols and colours mean. Click for more.
g.text: a bug through the fix loop

The map is one open ring: read it clockwise from Task at the top, round to the Run report. The gap at the top says a run ends; the next one is yours to start. Loops and spurs bend inside the ring. Hexagons are ants (AI agents), pages are files, dashed lines are side branches, and colour means something: green done, red failed, yellow warning. Click anything to learn what it is; Esc closes this panel."},{"y":600,"sub":[],"name":"Key","tip":"What the cars, symbols and colours mean.","src":"","id":"key","code":"","x":670,"about":"Left: what each numbered car shows. Right: the symbols: hexagon an ant, bin dropped, circle an interchange, stacked shapes parallel ants, dashed a side branch. Bottom: green done, red failed, yellow warning, blue plan, indigo build."},{"y":150,"sub":[],"name":"Part 1","tip":"1 ASK · 2 PLAN","src":"skills/ishikari/SKILL.md","id":"part-1","code":"","x":1670,"about":"Steps 1 and 2, the blue stretch from Task to the worker plans: the investigator asks you its questions, then the plan stage writes the design and one plan per task. The only part where you are asked anything."},{"y":1280,"sub":[],"name":"Part 2","tip":"3 BUILD · 4 CHECK · 5 FIX · 6 MERGE","src":"skills/ishikari/SKILL.md","id":"part-2","code":"","x":1670,"about":"Steps 3 to 5 and the first half of step 6, the indigo stretch down the right and along the bottom: worker ants build the plans in parallel, detective ants check each one and plan fixes, the integrator tests all passing tasks together, then the merger lands them in a scratch copy and the janitor cleans up. Main has not moved yet."},{"y":1280,"sub":[],"name":"Part 3","tip":"6 FINISH: JUDGE · MAIN MOVES","src":"skills/ishikari/SKILL.md","id":"part-3","code":"","x":30,"about":"Step 6, second half, up the left side: the judge scores the run against the plans, the docs ant updates the docs, the finisher moves main forward and runs the check, the retrospective ant reviews the run, and the run is reported."},{"y":445.9,"sub":[],"name":"Plan line","tip":"The first stretch of the ring: from your task to the worker plans.","src":"","id":"line-plan","code":"","x":1309.1,"about":"The blue line carries one task from Task through the investigator, its report, its design and its worker plans, and on to the worker ants, where building starts."},{"y":128.3,"sub":[],"name":"Question line","tip":"The investigator asks you, you answer.","src":"","id":"line-ask","code":"","x":1124.0,"about":"The investigator's questions go up to you and your answers come back as messages to the same live agent. The dot riding it is one round of questions."},{"y":329.6,"sub":[],"name":"Research line","tip":"The investigator sends researcher ants.","src":"","id":"line-res","code":"","x":1075.2,"about":"Up to 5 researcher ants at once look things up and report back down this line while the investigator waits. The dot riding it is one burst of research."},{"y":1157.4,"sub":["a plan may run a saved workflow in place of a worker ant","built: the script starts its detective at once","7+, or no gaps: no fix round"],"name":"Build line","tip":"The long stretch of the ring: build, check, merge, judge, finish.","src":"","id":"line-g1","code":"","x":622.0,"about":"The indigo trunk carries every task from the worker ants through checking, the combined test, the merge, the cleanup and the judge to MAIN. The numbered cars on it are worker tasks."},{"y":867.5,"sub":["bugs: the detective's fix plan goes back to the worker;","the worker builds it, the detective re-checks; 3 tries per bug"],"name":"Fix loop","tip":"A bug goes back to the worker and is re-checked.","src":"","id":"line-fix","code":"","x":1230.6,"about":"Yellow means a warning: the detective found a bug and planned its fix. The worker builds the fix and the detective re-checks, up to 3 tries per bug and 3 fix rounds."},{"y":946.0,"sub":["fail: tasks clash: the task takes them in, then the fix loop; 2 rounds"],"name":"Clash line","tip":"Tasks that break together go back to the fix loop.","src":"","id":"line-clash","code":"","x":1088.7,"about":"When the integrator's combined test shows two passing tasks clash, the task takes in the tasks it clashes with and goes back through the fix loop. 2 rounds at most."},{"y":878.4,"sub":[],"name":"Dropped spur","tip":"A task that could not be fixed leaves here.","src":"","id":"line-drop","code":"","x":1140.1,"about":"A task drops when a bug is still open after 3 tries, when 3 fix rounds end with bugs open (both: escalated), when its worker is blocked or hits an error, or when its after names a task that dropped: tasks built on it drop too. The main session drops it without asking; it never reaches finish or main and nothing sends it back. Its branch is kept for a later look, and the final report lists it with why it dropped, its bugs and fix history."},{"y":1119.0,"sub":[],"name":"Merge failed spur","tip":"A failed merge goes back to the worker ants.","src":"","id":"line-mback","code":"","x":880.0,"about":"A conflict, failed tests, or a task git cannot find goes back to the worker ant on its own branch: it merges main and fixes it, then the detective, integrator and merger run again. At most 2 extra build rounds."},{"y":1049.0,"sub":[],"name":"Cleanup failed spur","tip":"A failed cleanup becomes a suggested next task.","src":"","id":"line-tnext","code":"","x":760.5,"about":"If the janitor's tests fail, main moves with the tasks alone, the cleanup branch is kept, and its note is offered as the Task of the next run."},{"y":780.0,"sub":["below 7 and gaps: one fix round","a failed fix keeps its branch; the verdict says why"],"name":"Judge fix loop","tip":"Below 7 with gaps: one fix round.","src":"","id":"line-jfix","code":"","x":460.3,"about":"Yellow means a warning: the judge scored the run below 7 and listed gaps. You confirm once. The main session then edits on a branch in a worktree, runs the test and check commands, fast-forwards main only when both pass and logs it through ishikari.py. If it turns out bigger or a check keeps failing, the edits are thrown away and the full plan runs, told why."},{"y":762.4,"sub":[],"name":"Junction","tip":"Where the judge fix loop rejoins the line.","src":"","id":"junction-jfix-end","code":"","x":335.1,"about":"Not a station: the point where the judge fix loop rejoins. Yellow means a warning: the judge scored the run below 7 and listed gaps. A worker closes them, a detective checks, the merger fast-forwards the fix, and the judge scores again. Only one round."},{"y":181.4,"sub":["you give it, or a","dropped cleanup plan"],"name":"Task","tip":"The work you hand Ishikari.","src":"SKILL.md#1-setup","id":"task","code":"s1","x":958.1,"about":"Your task in your own words, or the note of a cleanup the last run dropped. Setup makes the run's state folder and env first; the main checkout must be on the main branch with no uncommitted changes."},{"y":249.0,"sub":["one live agent on Fable at max effort: it asks you,","proves the task can be built, designs it","and writes every worker plan; no other ant plans"],"name":"Investigator ant","tip":"Asks you questions, then designs the task and writes every plan.","src":"assets/prompts/investigator.md, SKILL.md#2a-investigate","id":"investigator","code":"s2","x":1125.6,"about":"One live agent run by the skill, not a workflow, on Fable at max effort; every other ant runs on Opus at low effort. It reads the repo once and gets each answer as a message. Part 1: it critiques the task, finds the test command, asks up to 4 independent questions at a time, 8 in all, writes the investigation report and judges whether the task is trivial. Part 2, when told to go on: it proves the task can be built, writes architecture.md and one plan per worker ant, and may ask you again when the design needs a choice. No other ant plans, so nothing is lost between ants. It stays alive until its plans pass the check or a fast path lands. Ishikari needs the Agent tool for it."},{"y":128.3,"sub":["up to 4 questions a round (/ask-simple),","8 in all; answering approves the whole run"],"name":"You","tip":"You answer the investigator's questions.","src":"SKILL.md#2a-live-investigator","id":"you","code":"s3","x":1124.0,"about":"The only time Ishikari asks you anything. Questions come through /ask-simple, up to 4 at a time, about 8 in all. Answering approves the whole run, merge to main included."},{"y":329.6,"sub":["up to 5 at once, web + computer,","read only; the investigator waits"],"name":"Researcher ants","tip":"Look up facts for the investigator.","src":"SKILL.md#limits","id":"researchers","code":"s4","x":1075.2,"about":"Up to 5 at once, on Opus at low effort. They search the web and the whole computer, read only, never secrets, and report back. The investigator starts them and waits for them. They are not logged."},{"y":369.9,"sub":["written when nothing is unclear;","then the trivial verdict, then the design"],"name":"investigation_report.md","tip":"Everything learned while planning, written once.","src":"<state>/plans/<run>/investigation_report.md","id":"report","code":"s5","x":1259.8,"about":"Goal, scope, every decision you made, facts with sources, constraints, risks, assumptions, acceptance checks and commands. Every claim cites an answer, a fact or the repo. Later ants read it instead of asking you. The main session never edits it. Once it is written the investigator gives its trivial verdict, then goes on to the design."},{"y":529.3,"sub":["the investigator's design: parts, files,","and every name and interface between parts;","not buildable: it asks you, or the run stops"],"name":"architecture.md","tip":"The investigator's design, so parallel workers fit together.","src":"<state>/plans/<run>/architecture.md","id":"design","code":"s6","x":1344.5,"about":"Written by the investigator after the report, once it has proved the task can be built from the repo's code and docs (a throwaway spike outside the repo only if needed). It names the parts of the change, the files each part owns, and every name, interface and data shape that crosses between parts, and maps each acceptance check to the part that proves it. If the task cannot be built as asked it asks you; only when no answer can fix it, the run stops. Detectives treat a name or interface that differs from it as a bug."},{"y":708.1,"sub":["one per task, written by the investigator;","the plan script checks them before anything is built;","problems go back to the investigator once"],"name":"Worker plans","tip":"One complete plan per task.","src":"<state>/plans/<run>/<task>.md","id":"plans","code":"s7","x":1369.7,"about":"Written by the investigator. Workers cannot ask questions, so each plan is complete: title, files, after. The plan script, which runs no ant, rejects bad or unknown ids, loops in after, two tasks on one file and paths outside the repo, before anything is built. Problems go back to the investigator once; still wrong, the run stops."},{"y":884.8,"sub":["max 5, one worktree each,","code + tests + docs;","stuck: next fix round"],"name":"Worker ants","tip":"Build the plans, one worktree each.","src":"scripts/ishikari-build.js","id":"workers","code":"s8","x":1332.1,"about":"Up to 5 at a time, each in its own git worktree. Writes code, tests and the docs its change affects, decides on its own and commits all its work. A worker that gets stuck says why, and that becomes a bug for the next fix round. A plan may name a saved workflow to run instead."},{"y":1051.2,"sub":["one per built task: checks it against plan +","design, runs tests (reuses the worker's if clean);","finds each bug's cause and plans its fix"],"name":"Detective ants","tip":"Check each built task and plan every fix.","src":"scripts/ishikari-build.js","id":"detectives","code":"s9","x":1224.1,"about":"One per task, started as soon as it is built. Checks the work against its plan and architecture.md, and runs the tests. Each bug comes back with how to see it, its cause and a fix plan; a worker builds the fix and the detective re-checks. 3 tries per bug, 3 fix rounds, then the task drops. Never changes code. A dropped task's branch is kept for a later look, tasks built on it drop too, and the final report lists them."},{"y":1165.0,"sub":["merges passing tasks in a scratch","copy, tests once: the combined test;","fewer than 2 passing tasks: no combined test"],"name":"Integrator ant","tip":"Merges all passing tasks in a scratch copy and tests once.","src":"scripts/ishikari-build.js (Combined phase)","id":"integrator","code":"s10","x":1061.5,"about":"Two tasks can pass alone and break together. It merges every passing task in a straight line in a throwaway copy and runs the tests once. A clashing task takes in the tasks it clashes with and goes back through the fix loop; 2 rounds. Skipped with fewer than 2 passing tasks."},{"y":1208.7,"sub":["merges in a straight line in a scratch copy,","or reuses build's trial merge; then checks","its own merge with git cherry"],"name":"Merger ant","tip":"Merges the approved tasks for real, then checks with git; failures go back to the workers.","src":"scripts/ishikari-finish.js (Merge phase)","id":"merger","code":"s11","x":886.3,"about":"Adds every passing task's commits in a straight line, in dependency order, in a scratch copy, and tests once. It reuses build's trial merge when nothing moved. Then it checks its own merge with git cherry and counts changed lines with git diff --shortstat. Never touches main. A conflict, failed tests, or a task git finds missing goes back to the worker ant on its own branch: it merges the current main, fixes the bug, the detective re-checks, the integrator tests again, and finish retries the merge. Tasks that merged cleanly are not rebuilt. At most 2 extra build rounds; what is left drops and is reported."},{"y":1194.6,"sub":["cleans up dead code and mess itself: edits,","runs the tests, commits, lands it only if","they pass. Skipped under 100 changed lines;","a cleanup run has no janitor"],"name":"Janitor ant","tip":"Cleans up mess the run left, by itself.","src":"scripts/ishikari-finish.js (Upkeep phase)","id":"janitor","code":"s12","x":724.2,"about":"Finds dead code, bloat and duplication from the merged tasks only. In its own worktree it edits, runs the tests and commits, and lands the cleanup only if they pass. Skipped under 100 changed lines, and a cleanup run gets no janitor. Tests failing: the cleanup is dropped, main moves with the tasks alone, its branch is kept, and its note goes to the next run's Task, where the investigator may ask about it."},{"y":1157.4,"sub":["one per merged task, 5 at once;","only with 3+ merged tasks"],"name":"Juror ants","tip":"Score each merged task against its plan.","src":"scripts/ishikari-finish.js","id":"jurors","code":"s13","x":622.0,"about":"One per merged task, up to 5 at once, only with 3 or more merged tasks. Each scores its task against that task's plan, and the judge weighs their reports."},{"y":1099.8,"sub":["scores the run 0-10: does the code","match the plans? its own call, not an average"],"name":"Judge ant","tip":"Scores the whole run 0-10 against the plans.","src":"scripts/ishikari-finish.js","id":"judge","code":"s14","x":529.9,"about":"Reads the investigation report, architecture and every worker plan, and the merged code with the cleanup on top. One question: does the code match the plans? The score is its own call, not an average. Below 7 with gaps: one fix round, then a second score. Main always moves; a score still below 7 is flagged in the report."},{"y":958.2,"sub":["closes the judge's gaps"],"name":"Worker ant","tip":"Closes the judge's gaps.","src":"scripts/ishikari-finish.js","id":"judge-fix-worker","code":"s15","x":563.2,"about":"Builds the judge's gaps as one fix on top of the merged scratch copy."},{"y":907.6,"sub":["checks the fix, runs the tests"],"name":"Detective ant","tip":"Checks the judge fix.","src":"scripts/ishikari-finish.js","id":"judge-fix-detective","code":"s16","x":533.9,"about":"Checks the fix and runs the tests. A failed fix keeps its branch and the verdict says why."},{"y":854.9,"sub":["fast-forwards the scratch copy to the fix;","the fix lands only through this fast-forward"],"name":"Merger ant","tip":"Lands the judge fix by fast-forward.","src":"scripts/ishikari-finish.js (merger-ant:judge-fix)","id":"judge-fix-merger","code":"s17","x":503.6,"about":"Fast-forwards the scratch copy to the fix. The fix lands only through this fast-forward."},{"y":804.3,"sub":["scores again; still below 7:","main moves, verdict flagged"],"name":"Judge ant","tip":"Scores again after the fix.","src":"scripts/ishikari-finish.js","id":"judge-again","code":"s18","x":474.3,"about":"Scores the run a second time. Still below 7: main moves anyway and the verdict is flagged. The judge never blocks main."},{"y":690.0,"sub":["updates the docs with /docs (update mode), last,","on the final code; lands only docs files, and only","if the docs check and tests pass; no docs folder: nothing to do"],"name":"Docs ant","tip":"Updates the repo's docs for the merged tasks, last, on the final code.","src":"scripts/ishikari-finish.js (Upkeep phase)","id":"docs","code":"s19","x":330.0,"about":"Runs the /docs skill in update mode on the merged scratch copy, in its own worktree. It changes only files under docs/ or doc/ and Markdown or Org files elsewhere, never code, tests or data, and never asks the user: open questions go in the docs' Open questions chapter. It runs docs/build.sh diagrams and check when present, then the tests, and fast-forwards the scratch copy only if all pass. The script refuses the landing if a changed file is not a docs file, and a refused or failed update is put back on the scratch copy. No docs/ or doc/ folder: it does nothing, since create mode needs the user. Failed: its branch is kept and main moves without it."},{"y":564.2,"sub":["fast-forwards main to the checked commit,","removes worktrees, appends the stage rows, runs the check"],"name":"Finisher ant","tip":"Moves main, cleans up, runs the check.","src":"scripts/ishikari-finish.js (Main phase)","id":"finisher","code":"s20","x":345.4,"about":"Fast-forwards main to the last checked commit, never to a branch by name; git refuses if it would overwrite local edits. A retry sees main already moved and carries on. Removes the worktrees, appends the stage's logbook rows, and runs checkCommand when it is set."},{"y":445.9,"sub":["fast-forward only,","never pushed"],"name":"MAIN","tip":"Your main branch, moved forward.","src":"SKILL.md#4-finish","id":"main","code":"s21","x":390.9,"about":"Moves only as a fast-forward, never a merge commit, and is never pushed. Push it yourself when you are happy."},{"y":328.8,"sub":["the finisher ant builds and checks the app,","only when main moved and checkCommand is set"],"name":"checkCommand","tip":"Builds and checks the app after main moves.","src":"ishikari.py config <state> checkCommand <cmd>","id":"check","code":"s22","x":475.9,"about":"The finisher ant runs the repo's saved checkCommand, only when main moved and the command is set. A failure starts one check-fix round. The check-fix round is one build round from the moved main, as a new task named check-fix. If the check still fails after it, the run stops and reports the output."},{"y":239.7,"sub":["reviews how this run went, read only;","writes retrospective.md: ranked fixes","to the Ishikari flow; never after a fast path"],"name":"Retrospective ant","tip":"Reviews how this run went and suggests fixes to the Ishikari flow. Read only.","src":"scripts/ishikari-retro.js","id":"retro","code":"s23","x":590.0,"about":"Runs once, as the very last step of every full run, however it ended: main moved, stopped, blocked or error; never after a fast path. It reads this run's logbook, the plans folder (report, architecture, plans, cleanup note, every stage result), the run's git history and Ishikari's own source. It looks for bugs, errors, wasted or repeated ant calls, retries, dead ants, slow stages, misleading plans or prompts, weak checks and missing steps, each backed by evidence from the run. It writes retrospective.md in the run's plans folder, ranked costliest first, each finding naming the Ishikari file and rule to change. box.querySelector('p.sum').textContent=(d.sub||[]).join(' ');box.querySelector('p.about').textContent=d.about; box.querySelector('code').textContent=d.src;box.querySelector('code').style.display=d.src?'':'none';pn.classList.add('on'); var ax=px==null?d.x:px,ay=py==null?d.y:py,h=box.offsetHeight||200,x=ax+30,y=ay-20; if(x+420>W-10)x=ax-450;if(x<10)x=10;if(y+h>H-10)y=H-10-h;if(y<10)y=10; pn.setAttribute('x',x);pn.setAttribute('y',y);pn.setAttribute('height',h+4);} function at(e){var p=svg.createSVGPoint();p.x=e.clientX;p.y=e.clientY;return p.matrixTransform(svg.getScreenCTM().inverse());} function hide(){pn.classList.remove('on');} document.querySelectorAll('.ck').forEach(function(g){ g.addEventListener('click',function(e){e.stopPropagation();var p=at(e);show(+g.dataset.i,p.x,p.y);});
